title: Food Nutrients
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 5 Agriculture; not yet checked by a CBC Agriculture teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Talk about food and illness kindly: some children in class may know hunger. Say these diseases come from food the body lacks, never from a family's fault.

skills.key_step: The child explains what each nutrient does: carbohydrates and fats give energy, proteins build and repair the body, vitamins and minerals protect and regulate it, water carries and cools, and roughage helps digestion.
representations: a nutrient chart with food pictures
steps: Say its job in the body.
Name a food rich in it.
contexts: a breakfast of tea and bread

board.do: Ask which builds and repairs the body.
Write "protein: growth and repair; carbohydrate: energy".

misconceptions.ask: Which nutrient builds and repairs the body?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what a growing child needs to make new muscle.

misconceptions.ask: What do vitamins do in the body?
misconceptions.repair: Ask which group of foods stops illness.

misconceptions.ask: What is one job of fats in the body?
misconceptions.repair: Ask why animals in cold places have a layer of fat.

listen_for: It does not; only food matters
misconceptions.ask: Why does the body need water?
misconceptions.repair: Ask how you feel after games on a hot day with no water.

checks.question: What is the main job of proteins?
checks.answer: to build and repair the body

checks.question: Which nutrient helps food pass through the gut?

skills.key_step: The child sorts foods by their main nutrient: carbohydrates (maize, rice, cassava, potatoes), proteins (beans, meat, eggs, milk, fish), fats and oils, vitamins and minerals (fruits and vegetables).
steps: Ask what it is mostly made of.
Put it in its nutrient group.

board.do: Draw five boxes for the nutrient groups.
Write oil in Fats and oils.

misconceptions.repair: Ask what ugali, rice and cassava have in common.

misconceptions.ask: Which group is an egg in?

misconceptions.repair: Ask what ugali is made from and what it gives for running and playing.

misconceptions.ask: Which nutrient is cooking oil rich in?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what is left on the pan after frying.

checks.question: What is the main nutrient in beans?
Which group are kale and oranges in?

skills.key_step: The child identifies nutritional diseases and their cause: kwashiorkor (too little protein: swollen belly and legs), marasmus (too little of all food: very thin), anaemia (too little iron), goitre (too little iodine), rickets (too little vitamin D and calcium), scurvy (too little vitamin C), night blindness (too little vitamin A).
representations: a story of a clinic visit

board.do: Write "goitre: a swelling in the neck".

misconceptions.ask: A very thin child with little muscle has had too little food overall. Which disease is this?
misconceptions.repair: Describe the pictures: a swollen belly and puffy legs, and a very thin wasted child.

misconceptions.ask: Can anaemia from lack of iron spread from one child to another?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what two children from the same home both ate and what they both missed.

misconceptions.ask: A swelling at the front of the neck can come from too little of which mineral?
misconceptions.repair: Match each disease with its missing nutrient on a card.
Show which foods and what sunlight build strong bones.

checks.question: Which disease is caused by too little protein?
Lack of iron leads to which condition?

skills.key_step: The child chooses foods and habits that prevent nutritional diseases: a balanced diet every day, iodised salt, fruits and vegetables, milk and small fish, breastfeeding babies, and visiting the clinic.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the nutritional diseases and their causes.
floor.question: What causes goitre?

representations: packets of iodised salt and plain salt
steps: Name the food that prevents it.
Add it to a balanced meal.

board.do: Wait for carrots, pawpaw, green vegetables.

listen_for: Only ugali, as much as they want
misconceptions.ask: Which meal protects a family best from nutritional diseases?
misconceptions.repair: Ask which nutrients ugali alone is missing.

listen_for: Any salt, even if it has no iodine
misconceptions.repair: Check the packet for the word iodised.
Ask what a family can do at the next meal.

misconceptions.ask: Do sweets and soda prevent nutritional diseases?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a soda with milk on a nutrient chart: which has protein and calcium?

checks.question: How can a family prevent kwashiorkor cheaply?
checks.answer: add beans, ndengu, eggs or milk to meals
